chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not eat the meat of the jallalah, and if its sweat touches you, wash it."

key_terms.اللُّحُومَ الْجَلَّالَةَ: Meat of animals fed on impure excrement or waste

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating jallalah meat and washing its sweat?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of *jallalah*—animals fed on impure waste—as having meat that is not strictly haram but is disliked (*makruh*) or prohibited depending on the school of thought, while mandating the washing of sweat to maintain ritual purity. It highlights the Shia emphasis on both the physical and spiritual cleanliness of food sources, linking dietary habits to bodily purity in worship.
